title: From Bhindi to Chicken Leg: Six Viral Samosa Variations That Marked World Samosa Day
excerpt: World Samosa Day on September 5 brought out the internet's wildest takes on India's favorite triangular snack — some brilliant, some bewildering.
body:
• World Samosa Day, celebrated on September 5, sparked a wave of viral samosa variation videos across Indian social media.
  • Standout creations include the chicken leg piece samosa, Maggi noodle samosa, thread samosa, and the polarizing bhindi (okra) samosa.
  • The classic aloo samosa remains dominant, but food creators and street vendors are pushing the boundaries with increasingly experimental fillings.

The samosa needs no introduction. The deep-fried triangular pastry stuffed with spiced potato is the default snack at Indian tea stalls, canteens, offices, and family gatherings. But World Samosa Day on September 5 brought out the internet's experimental side, with food creators and street vendors showcasing variations that ranged from inspired to deeply questionable, according to NDTV Food.

The Chicken Leg Piece Samosa

This one turns heads for its visual alone. A seasoned chicken leg is placed on a maida sheet with masala filling, wrapped into a samosa shape with the bone end sticking out, and deep-fried until golden. The result is part samosa, part lollipop — crunchy on the outside, juicy within. It is impractical, messy, and by most accounts delicious.

The Maggi Samosa

"As one commenter summed it up: "Ab wo din gaye jab samosa me aalo hua karta tha" — gone are the days when samosas simply had potato."

For a country that puts Maggi noodles in everything from dosa to sandwiches, stuffing them into a samosa was inevitable. Cooked and seasoned Maggi replaces the traditional potato filling, and the whole thing is folded and fried until crisp. It brings together two of India's most beloved snack foods in a single package.

The Bhindi Samosa

This one divided the internet. Videos of vendors selling samosas stuffed with okra instead of potato went viral, drawing reactions that ranged from curiosity to outrage. "Justice for bhindi and samosa," one commenter wrote, while another pleaded: "Band karo aap ise please." The bhindi samosa is a reminder that not all innovation is welcome — but it gets people talking.

The Thread Samosa

A variation that replaces the traditional maida shell with fine threads of fried dough, giving the samosa a bird's-nest-like exterior. The filling stays classic — spiced potato — but the textural contrast between the lacy, shatteringly crisp shell and the soft interior elevates the experience.

More Variations Making the Rounds

The list does not stop there. Croissant samosas blend French pastry technique with Indian filling. Pizza samosas, chocolate samosas, and butter chicken samosas have all surfaced in metros from Mumbai to Toronto. A vendor in Jalandhar, Punjab, went viral for offering more than 200 samosa varieties, including noodles, manchurian, and chilli potato versions.

The Enduring Appeal of the Original

World Samosa Day is celebrated on September 5 each year, and the samosa's origins trace back centuries — Central Asian traders brought an early version called the "sanbosag" to India, where it evolved into the spiced-potato pocket that defines Indian street food today.

For all the viral experiments, the original aloo samosa remains unchallenged. As one commenter summed it up: "Ab wo din gaye jab samosa me aalo hua karta tha" — gone are the days when samosas simply had potato. But for millions, those days are still going strong.
